correctness.rationale: A five-point cap would use all four lines through every one of its points to meet its four other points. Then no line meets it once, and the four lines through an exterior point partition the five points into subsets of even size, a contradiction. Two colours cannot cover nine points by caps, and valid three-colour assignments exist. Inclusion–exclusion over subsets of the 12 monochromatic-line events uses q to the number of equivalence classes forced by selected lines; all 4096 subsets independently gave nonzero (degree, coefficient) pairs (9,1),(7,−12),(5,66),(4,−72),(3,−4),(2,27),(1,−6), with the stated factorization. The independent implementation tested every named word of length nine, generated all 432 affine maps and six palette permutations, and performed BFS from every state with edges exactly the proper single-point changes. It reproduced 3762 vertices, 16848 edges, and orbit (size, sorted class sizes, rainbow signature, degree, eccentricity) rows (144,333,0003,9,10), (162,144,0000,8,10), (864,333,0111,9,9), (1296,234,0002,9,9), (1296,234,0011,9,9). All searches reached all vertices. Each of exactly 306 peripheral states has two distance-ten antipodes, producing exactly 306 unordered diametral pairs; the full unordered histogram also matches. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/6d4f8982-35b5-444e-9a4a-3c5d8b945a3e/verify_independent.py; its exact output is independent_run.txt in that directory. Supplied checker sources were inspected, not run. The argument exhausts the stated plane, palette and move rule; it is not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: This smallest affine plane with triple lines is a canonical symmetric test of optimal weak-colouring dynamics, not a specially selected input graph. Connectivity, exact worst-case change count and antipode multiplicity distinguish the metric from mere feasibility. Recovering the extremal states from intrinsic colour-class and parallel-rainbow structure makes the census useful for questions about small symmetric reconfiguration spaces; the polynomial and complete orbit table provide coherent exact baselines. No higher-order conclusion is assumed.
